item.title: Makoi residents call for more Police patrols after attempted break-in
item.description: Residents along Vula Street in Makoi are concerned about their safety and are calling for increased police patrols after a man allegedly climbed onto the roof of a house and tried to find a way inside last night. This follows another break-in in the neighbourhood last week.
item.content:encoded:
Residents along Vula Street in Makoi are concerned about their safety and are calling for increased police patrols after a man allegedly climbed onto the roof of a house and tried to find a way inside last night.

This follows another break-in in the neighbourhood last week.

A resident , says the incident happened sometime after 10pm while it was raining heavily.

She says she initially heard noise outside and went around the house switching on the lights in different rooms as she tried to work out where it was coming from.

S he says when she and her grandmother went towards the front of their house and shop, some neighbourhood boys who were already outside alerted them that someone was at the house.

She says the man was on the roof and appeared to be trying to find a way into the house.

The resident says because of the heavy rain, they were unable to immediately check the roof to determine whether the man had left any tools or had attempted to remove anything.

She says the man later jumped from the roof, while some neighbourhood boys jumped over a neighbour's fence into their compound and managed to catch him.

Resident says no one in the household was injured as they were safely inside the house during the incident.

She says neighbours had already contacted Police, who arrived about five minutes later and took the man away.

She says when she later went to give her statement, the man was still at the Police station, adding that he appeared to have been drunk.

She says she has lived in the area for about 25 years and has never experienced anything like this before.

She says she also learnt that there had reportedly been another break-in near the roundabout recently, and is raising concerns as this would be the second such incident in the neighbourhood within a week.

She says residents are now worried about their safety and would like to see increased Police patrols in the area.

She says her family also operates a shop, which adds to their concerns, as they do not know what could have happened if the man had managed to enter the house.

We have contacted Police for further information.

item.title: 126 students and teachers from special and inclusive schools unite to make history through song
item.description: Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro, described the participation as a significant milestone for special and inclusive education in Fiji. He says the opportunity allows students to showcase their talents, build confidence and take part meaningfully in the wider community.
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro, described the participation as a significant milestone for special and inclusive education in Fiji.

He says the opportunity allows students to showcase their talents, build confidence and take part meaningfully in the wider community.

Radrodro acknowledged the Methodist Church in Fiji and Rotuma for providing the opportunity, as well as the Fiji Council of Special and Inclusive Educators, the Fiji Disabled Persons Federation, parents, teachers, school leaders and other organisations for their continued support.

He also praised the students and teachers for their dedication and commitment to the competition.

The students have been practising separately at their respective schools and coordinating their performances through a Viber group before coming together as one choir.

The Minister says the students’ participation demonstrates that, when provided with the right opportunities, encouragement and support, they can achieve their goals and make valuable contributions to society.

He says the performance will be the beginning of the Fiji Council of Special and Inclusive Educators Choir and create more opportunities for students to participate in singing, drama, dance, poetry and other creative activities.

He wished the students and teachers the very best for the competition, encouraging them to enjoy the experience, celebrate their talents and take pride in representing their schools and the special and inclusive education community. The Choir competition is at the Vodafone Arena at 4pm.

item.title: Drug abuse, teenage pregnancies among issues at Women’s Conference
item.description: The growing impact of drug abuse, teenage pregnancies, youth offending and violence against women will be among the issues highlighted during the Methodist Church in Fiji and Rotuma Women’s Conference on Tuesday. An awareness session will be held as part of the one-day conference programme at the World Harvest Centre, bringing together women from the 59 divisions of the Methodist Church in Fiji an
item.content:encoded:
The growing impact of drug abuse, teenage pregnancies, youth offending and violence against women will be among the issues highlighted during the Methodist Church in Fiji and Rotuma Women’s Conference on Tuesday.

An awareness session will be held as part of the one-day conference programme at the World Harvest Centre, bringing together women from the 59 divisions of the Methodist Church in Fiji and Rotuma.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Secretary for the Methodist Women’s Fellowship (MWF), Reverend Maraia Toko says the session will focus on the theme, “Women of Faith Responding to Social Issues”.

She says the CEO of the Substance Abuse Advisory Council Josua Naisele, who will be the guest speaker, is expected to raise awareness about some of the challenges affecting families and communities.

Reverend Toko says particular attention will be given to rising drug use and its impact on children and young people, teenage pregnancies , youth offending, and the abuse and harassment faced by women.

She says the aim is for women attending the session to better understand these issues and take what they have learned back to their families, churches and communities.

Women from three age groups within the Methodist Church will participate in the programme, including the Ruci Group for women aged 20 to 40, the Priscilla Group for those aged 41 to 50, and the Sera Group for women aged 51 to 60.

The programme will be held on Tuesday from 8am to 1pm and will also include praise and worship, as well as a combined prayer service.

Today, members of the church held a march from John Wesley College to the Vodafone Arena to mark the beginning of the Methodist Church Annual Conference.

Church members turned up in numbers to be part of this auspicious occasion.

item.title: Sustaining skilled personnel remains Fiji Navy’s biggest challenge - Navy Commander
item.description: The biggest challenge facing the Fiji Navy is sustaining its people and keeping them in the service as more opportunities become available for personnel with specialised skills. Republic of Fiji Navy Commander, Commodore Timoci Natuva says while the Navy continues to improve its technology and capabilities, its people remain the priority.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest challenge facing the Fiji Navy is sustaining its people and keeping them in the service as more opportunities become available for personnel with specialised skills.

Republic of Fiji Navy Commander, Commodore Timoci Natuva says while the Navy continues to improve its technology and capabilities, its people remain the priority.

Commodore Natuva says recruiting people is easy, but sustaining them is a challenge, particularly in terms of pay and allowances.

He says the Navy is working to ensure its personnel are looked after and their welfare is taken care of.

Commodore Natuva says some personnel have resigned in recent years for opportunities in Australia, New Zealand and the United States.

He says others have moved to agencies and companies in Fiji, including Airports Fiji Limited and shipping companies.

Commodore Natuva says despite improvements in technology and capability, sustaining their people and keeping them in the Navy remains their biggest challenge.
